description: Synthetic journal entries for tuning the mirror. group = shared idea (related). kind: idea | negative-topic (same topic, different idea) | negative-mood (same mood, different topic) | filler. Negatives have no group: any surfaced memory for them is a false positive. Idea-group pairs are the only related pairs.

entries.text: I realised tonight that scrolling my phone in bed is what keeps me awake. The blue glow and the endless little hooks mean my mind never winds down. I want to leave the phone charging in the kitchen and read a paper book instead.
Tried a new rule: no screens after ten. I put the phone across the room and felt twitchy for about twenty minutes, then fell asleep faster than I have in weeks.

Long day, mostly meetings and a late train. The sourdough starter finally rose properly, which cheered me up. Dinner was leftover soup. Something I keep coming back to is that my nights get ruined by the device beside my pillow; if I just banished it from the bedroom I would probably wake up rested. Anyway, the laundry still needs folding and I should call the plumber tomorrow.
Bedtime and my phone again. I keep grabbing it in the dark and an hour disappears. The fix is obvious: keep it out of reach of the bed.

I said something cruel to Maya at dinner about her career and I have been sick about it all day. I owe her an apology, a real one, not a text with a smiley face. I should call her tomorrow and just say I was wrong.
Still thinking about the thing I blurted out to my sister. Pride keeps getting in the way of saying sorry. Maybe the right move is to admit it plainly and ask how she felt.

Finally called Maya and apologised for the harsh words about her job. She went quiet and then said thank you. I feel lighter, like I put down something heavy I had been carrying for months. It turns out saying sorry is the easy part once you start.
The guitar practice has stalled. I can play the same four chords I could three months ago, and switching to barre chords still buzzes. It feels like I have hit a ceiling and I'm not improving at all.
Nothing seems to get better on the guitar. Every evening I repeat the same exercises and my fingers refuse to move faster. Progress has flatlined and I wonder whether I should even keep going.

Spent the weekend at my aunt's place, the garden was lovely and we had a picnic by the pond. On the drive home I thought about how my playing has been stuck in the same rut for ages, no noticeable improvement however much I practice, and how that discouragement is wearing on me.

I want a cushion in the bank equal to six months of expenses. If the job disappeared tomorrow I would panic, and a rainy-day fund would take most of that fear away. Setting up an automatic transfer on payday.
Checked the savings balance: three months of living costs set aside so far. Having a safety net for emergencies lets me sleep better. Aiming for double by next spring.
Money notes. Money should be building a buffer against surprises, a stash I never touch except for real emergencies like losing work or a big medical bill.
The offer in Lisbon is real. Part of me is thrilled, but leaving everyone I know and starting from zero in a new country scares me more than I want to admit. What if I move and I'm lonely?
Packing boxes in my head. Relocating abroad means no friends nearby, a different language, and building a whole life again. I am excited and terrified at the same time about the move.
I keep drafting the email accepting the overseas job and then closing the laptop. The unknown city, the strangers, giving up my familiar routines, that is what is stopping me.
I signed up for my first ten kilometre race in October. I never thought I could run that far. Today I managed six without stopping and nearly cried at the end, I was so proud.
Long run this morning: eight kilometres, slow and steady. Training for the 10k race is starting to feel possible, my legs are stronger and my breathing is easier.
Race day tomorrow, my first ever 10K. Nervous but ready. I plan to start slowly and not get carried away by the crowd.
My manager told me in front of the team that my report was sloppy. I had worked on it for two weeks and nobody had mentioned any problems before. It felt unfair and public, and I am still angry.
Replaying the review meeting. The criticism came out of nowhere, delivered with an audience, and it ignored everything I did well. I want to ask for private feedback next time.
That humiliating moment when my boss called out my work in the all-hands keeps haunting me. The critique wasn't even accurate. Why do I carry unfair comments for so long?
I have to present to the whole department on Friday and my stomach is in knots. My voice shakes, my hands sweat, and I forget what I wanted to say the moment people look at me.
Speaking in front of a room full of people terrifies me. I rehearsed my toast in the mirror and still blanked. I want to learn to stay calm when everyone is watching.
Volunteered for the conference talk and immediately regretted it. Standing on a stage with all those faces staring back makes my heart race. Maybe practising in small groups first will help.
Autocomplete was hammering the API with a call for each letter typed. Fixed by delaying the call until the user pauses for a moment, using a small timer helper that resets on each keypress.
Reminder to self: throttle the type-ahead lookups so that we only query once the person stops typing. Otherwise every character triggers a network request.
Day three without sweets. I get headaches around four o'clock and reach for biscuits out of habit. I want to break the sugar cravings once and for all.
Two weeks off sugar and I notice my energy is steadier. The afternoon crash is gone and I'm not craving desserts the way I used to.
Slipped today and ate half a chocolate cake. The urge for something sweet hits hardest when I'm tired. Cutting out sugar is harder than I expected, but I'm starting again tomorrow.
Found my grandmother's handwritten recipe cards in a tin. The stains and the faded ink made me tear up. I want to cook every one of them so her kitchen stays alive somewhere.
Made nana's lentil soup from her old index card tonight. The smell took me straight back to her small flat. Cooking her dishes is how I keep her close.
I want to type up the recipes my grandma left behind before the paper falls apart, so the family can keep making her food for years.
Bought a new mattress today, a medium-firm hybrid. The delivery guys carried it up three flights and the old one is going to the tip on Saturday. Hopefully my back appreciates it.
Woke at three to a neighbour's car alarm and could not get back to sleep. Earplugs are on the shopping list.
Maya came over for brunch and we laughed about our childhood road trips. She is thinking about repainting her flat green.
Snapped a string on the guitar and had to walk to the music shop. The owner restrung it and told me about a vintage Fender in the window. Lovely little shop.
Spent too long choosing a birthday present for Tom. Ended up with a nice pen and a notebook, around forty pounds, and wrapped it badly.
My friend Lena just moved to Berlin and sent photos of her tiny balcony. The movers lost a lamp but otherwise it went well.
Watched the marathon on television this morning. The leaders looked almost effortless. Someone dressed as a banana won the fancy-dress category.
Spent the afternoon figuring out why a SQL query was slow. Adding a composite index on user_id and created_at brought it from four seconds to forty milliseconds.
My manager brought in a cake for the team's anniversary and gave a short, warm speech. We all clapped. The lemon sponge was excellent.
Went to a talk about urban beekeeping at the library. The speaker was funny and handed out honey samples. I learned queens can live five years.
Read an article on how sugar was once sold as medicine in the eighteenth century. Fascinating history, a bit gross.
Tried a new pasta with burnt butter and sage. Too salty, but the texture of the fresh gnocchi was great. Will use less salt next time.
Dentist tomorrow and I'm anxious, my mind keeps rehearsing the worst. I know it's silly but the waiting is awful.
Flying to Denver next week and I can't stop worrying about turbulence. I keep checking the forecast like it will change anything.
Sad today for no obvious reason. Grey sky, heavy chest. I made tea and sat by the window watching the rain slide down.
Proud of myself for finally fixing the leaking tap on my own. Watched a video, borrowed a wrench, done in an hour.
Feeling frustrated with the neighbours' loud renovation. Drilling from nine till five and I cannot concentrate on anything.
Rainy Tuesday. Bought milk, eggs and bread. The bus was late again and I got soaked.
Watched two episodes of that detective show. The ending was predictable but I enjoyed the costumes.
Cleaned the bathroom, did three loads of laundry and finally replaced the lightbulb in the hallway. Not much else happened.
The office coffee machine broke so I walked to the cafe on the corner. Flat white, nice croissant, forty minutes to answer emails.
Sunny at last. Hung washing outside, watered the tomatoes, and chatted with the postman about the football.
Ordered takeaway noodles and watched a documentary about deep sea creatures. Bed by eleven.
Dentist appointment moved to next month. Renewed my library books and cleared out the junk drawer.
